points: This carryover audit supplements only G2 and G3; G0/G4/G5/G1 are inherited from the captured record.

A real Chrome session read both complete US-English pages without CAPTCHA. Page one mixes the new changelog, a daily.dev syndication, credential and token docs, revocation API references, prior revocation changes, credential-type reference and social reposts; page two falls into Marketplace cleanup, security news, support questions, repository copies and OAuth discussions.

G2=pass: the result set is fragmented across documentation inner pages, announcements, support and secondary reporting rather than a task-completing media/wiki/homepage takeover. The current AI Overview describes token classes and action semantics but does not provide the UI/API execution path.

GitHub's changelog plus linked enterprise and organization REST documentation form a complete official implementation set: token-type and user-specific bulk deauthorization/revocation, UI and API parity, permission requirements, audit logging and user notifications.

G3=pass: no second independent page completes the new token-type workflow. daily.dev and security-news pages restate the announcement, while generic credential revocation docs and older OAuth questions lack the new bulk token-type actions.
This is not veto_window_bet because no second built exact implementation is merely awaiting indexing.
Window estimate is weeks, expiring 2026-09-20. The feature is two days old, but GitHub's linked UI/API docs and syndication can close the gap quickly.

Invalidation conditions: two free independent token-type bulk revocation/deauthorization guides enter the SERP; GitHub publishes a dedicated incident-response tutorial; API version, endpoint, token-type set, permission model, audit events, or organization/enterprise parity changes.
